result.topic_en: Algebraic elimination in spherical trigonometry: from relations cos h = A cos e, sin h sin e = B, cos h cos e = C, Gauss derives a relation among A, B, C and applies it to formulas involving angles a, b, φ, δ.
result.transcription:
Aus [?] folgt
$\cos h = A\cos e$
$\sin h\sin e = B$
$\cos h\cos e = C$

$(1-xx)(1-yy) = BB$
$x = Ay$
$xy = C$

$1-xx-yy+CC = BB$
$1-(AA+1)yy$
$yy = \frac{1+CC-BB}{1+AA}$
$1-yy = \frac{CC-AA-BB}{1+AA}$
$xx = \frac{AA(1+CC-BB)}{1+AA}$
$CC = \frac{AA(1+CC-BB)}{(1+AA)^2}$

$\sin e\cos\varphi = \sin b$
$\frac{\mathrm{tg}\, a}{\cos b} = \frac{\cos\varphi}{\sin h}$

$(A-C)(1-AC) = ABB$
$BB = \left(1-\frac{C}{A}\right)(1-AC) = \left(A-C\right)\left(\frac{1}{A}-C\right)$

$B = -\frac{\cos a\sin b}{\cos\varphi\cos\delta}$

$C = \frac{\sin a\cos b - \sin\varphi\sin\delta}{\cos\varphi\cos\delta}$ $\quad \frac{\mathrm{tg}\,\delta}{\mathrm{tg}\,\varphi}$

$\cos a^2\sin b^2 = \sin a\cos b - \sin\varphi\sin\delta - \frac{\sin\delta\cos\varphi^2}{\sin\varphi}$
$\sin a\cos b - \sin\varphi\sin\delta - \frac{\sin\varphi\cos\delta^2}{\sin\delta}$

$C(1+AA) = A(1+CC-BB)$
$xy\left(1+\frac{xx}{yy}\right) = \frac{x}{y}\left(1+xxyy-(1-xx)(1-yy)\right)$

[figure: spherical triangle, labelled P]

$\frac{\sin a}{\cos b}+\frac{\cos b}{\sin a} = \frac{\sin\delta}{\sin\varphi}+\frac{\sin\varphi}{\sin\delta}$

$p+\frac{1}{p} = q+\frac{1}{q}$
$pp+1$
$(p-q)\left(1-\frac{1}{pq}\right)$
$(p-q)(pq-1)$

$\left(\sin a\cos b - \frac{\sin\delta}{\sin\varphi}\right)\left(\sin a\cos b - \frac{\sin\varphi}{\sin\delta}\right)$

$\cos a^2\sin b^2 = \sin a^2\cos b^2 + 1 - \sin a\cos b\frac{\sin\delta}{\sin\varphi} - \sin a\cos b\frac{\sin\varphi}{\sin\delta}$
$1-\sin a^2-\sin b^2+$
$\sin a^2+\cos b^2 = \sin a\cos b\left(\frac{\sin\delta}{\sin\varphi}+\frac{\sin\varphi}{\sin\delta}\right)$
